summary.short: Would amend the Defense Production Act to let the Treasury Secretary prohibit, and require notification of, US persons' covered investments in prohibited and notifiable technologies (including AI systems) in countries of concern; also authorizes IEEPA sanctions on covered foreign persons. Sunsets seven years after enactment.
summary.long: Introduced bill (S. 3555, 119th Congress) with five titles. Title II lets the President use IEEPA powers to prohibit US persons from investing in or buying significant equity or debt of covered foreign persons, a term tied to the People's Republic of China (including Hong Kong and Macau). Title III adds Title VIII to the Defense Production Act: the Treasury Secretary may prohibit covered national security transactions by US persons, including controlled foreign entities, in prohibited technologies, which include artificial intelligence systems. Notification of such transactions, and of transactions in notifiable technologies such as AI systems, is required within 30 days after completion, with regulations due within 450 days of enactment. Exemptions cover national-interest and intelligence activities, de minimis values and listed securities. Civil penalties follow IEEPA amounts, and the Secretary may compel divestment. Title VIII also requires reports and testimony to Congress, allows a non-exhaustive public database of covered foreign persons, and protects filed information from disclosure. Title IV requires presidential reports on the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List. The Act ceases to have effect seven years after enactment.

notes: Introduced bill text; the text records no legislative events. Internal inconsistencies: 'country of concern' is PRC only in Sec. 202(2) and Sec. 401(b)(2), but in new DPA Sec. 809(2) it also covers Cuba, Iran, DPRK, Russia and Venezuela. 'Covered foreign person' is defined in Sec. 202(3) with an added condition (F) (knowingly engaged in significant operations in defense or surveillance) that Sec. 809(3) does not contain. 'section 709' (Secs. 801(e)(1), 802(b)(1)) is not identified in the text. Sec. 803(e)(1) refers to 'amendments as described in subsection (a)(2)', but (a)(2) describes an assessment.
